standard.title: Dance across cultures and contexts
standard.description: explore where, why and how people across cultures, communities and/or other contexts experience dance
standard.prior_knowledge: Students have explored how arts are important for communities at Foundation. They recognise that arts experiences — including dances — bring people together and carry cultural meaning.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students explore where, why and how people across cultures, communities and/or other contexts experience dance.

nodes.label: Observing and describing dance
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can observe a dance and describe its features — movements, music, costume — using their own words and some dance terminology.
nodes.minimum_width: Observing at least one dance from a culture or context different from their own; describing what they notice using their own words.
nodes.typical_width: Observing and describing multiple dances using Viewpoints questions ('What movements?', 'What music?', 'What are they wearing?', 'What are they communicating?'); recognising and describing movement patterns; using a mix of own words and learnt terminology.
wider: View and compare two dances from different cultural contexts — identifying similarities and differences in movement, costume, music and setting
Share dances familiar from home and family, and compare with dances shared by peers — building a collective picture of dance diversity in the class community
nodes.hinge_reason: The ability to observe and describe dance features is the foundation for cultural and contextual understanding — without it, students cannot engage meaningfully with where, why and how dance occurs.

response_modes.reason: Viewpoints questioning scaffolds observation into description. Students need a lens for looking — provide structured prompts before asking open responses. Build vocabulary incrementally: movements → music → costume → purpose.

success_criteria: Student can describe at least two features of a dance they have observed (e.g. movements, music, costume)
Student uses at least one learnt dance term correctly in describing what they see

nodes.label: Where, why and how people dance
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify that people dance for different reasons in different places and contexts — and that dance can communicate feelings, knowledge and cultural identity.
nodes.minimum_width: Identifying at least two different contexts in which people dance (e.g. celebration, ceremony, entertainment) and one reason why dance is used in each.
nodes.typical_width: Exploring where, why and how dance is experienced: identifying cultural purposes (stories, traditions, ceremonies), recognising similarities and differences across dances, identifying how dance communicates feelings about places, people and experiences.
wider: Explore dances experienced with students' own families and communities — comparing purposes and traditions with dances experienced by peers
Investigate how dance communicates feelings about specific places or environments — connecting to students' own sense of belonging to place

response_modes.reason: Understanding that dance has many purposes and contexts requires encountering genuine diversity — not just acknowledging it exists. More cultural and contextual examples = richer understanding of dance's role in human life.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Students who encounter a genuine diversity of dance contexts and purposes develop a rich conceptual map of dance as a cultural practice — this supports respectful engagement with First Nations dance and all cross-cultural content throughout F-10.
success_criteria: Student can identify at least two different purposes for dance (e.g. celebration, storytelling, ceremony)
Student can explain that dance can communicate feelings about places, people or experiences
